text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT/BARLEY SALE - The Japanese Food Agency said on Thursday it had bought 100,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, 40,000 of Canadian no 1 western red spring wheat, 40,000 of Australian standad white wheat, 20,000 of Canadian feed barley and 20,000 of Australian barley at its weekly tender for January/February shipment. The U.S. wheat comprised 20,000 tonnes of western white, 36,000 tonnes of dark northern spring and 44,000 tonnes of hard red winter. The Australian barley comprised 10,000 tonnes of feed and 10,000 tonnes of food barley.

WHEAT SALES - South Korea's Cheiljedang Corp and Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd on Thursday bought a total of 21,500 tonnes of U.S. wheat from Marubeni Corp. Dongah bought 4,500 tonnes of soft white at $148.45 a tonne, 2,500 tonnes of soft white at $144.77 and 2,500 tonnes of hard red winter at $178.31. Cheiljedang Corp bought 500 tonnes of soft white at 33-3/4 cents over March CBOT futures, 800 tonnes of soft white at 23-3/4 over March CBOT, 6,200 tonnes of hard red winter at 96.27 cents over March KCBT futures and 4,500 tonnes dark northern spring at $1.25 over March MGE futures. Shipment was set for Feb 5-Mar 5 from the Pacific Northwest to Inchon.

WHEAT SALES (cont.) - Japanese trading house Nichimen Corp sold 6,000 tonnes of Austrailan wheat to a South Korean flour milling company, traders said on Thursday. They said the deal was made in a private negotiation between the two companies. Nichimen sold 1,000 tonnes of Australian soft wheat, 4,000 tonnes of Australian soft white wheat and 1,000 tonnes of Australian hard wheat to the South Korean company, they said. The identity of the South Korean company was not available. Shipment was slated for January 20-February 20 to the South Korean port city of Inchon.

WHEAT SALES (cont.) - Tunisia bought 100,000 tonnes of Argentine and optional soft wheat for January-February shipment at a tender on Thursday, traders said. The purchase comprised one lot of 25,000 tonnes of Argentine origin at $130.78 FOB per tonne for Jan 5-15 shipment, one lot of 25,000 tonnes of US, Argentine or EU origin at $152.83 C&F per tonne for shipment on Jan 15-25, one lot of 25,000 tonnes of U.S., Argentine, EU, or Australian origin for Feb 1-10 shipment.
LENTIL TENDER - Syria offered 9,500 tonnes of lentils for export. December 16 was set as final date for bids and results would be announced on December 17.

WHEAT TENDERS - The Egyptian state's General Authority for Supply Commodities (GASC) said on Thursday it was inviting bids for 50,000 tonnes of U.S., French, Australian or Argentine wheat for shipment in January of February. The deadline for bids is 0700 GMT on Saturday, December 7, and bids should be valid until 1100 GMT on Monday, GASC chairman Samir Shakankiri told Reuters. He said GASC was looking for any type of U.S. wheat, soft red French wheat, standard soft while Australian wheat or Argentine wheat. Shipment date will be at buyer's option, Shakankiri said.

WHEAT TENDERS - Sri Lanka is expected to soon seek 100,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat for delivery in January and February. Potential suppliers could include the United States, Argentina, Australian and Canada, European grain traders said.

- Turkey will invite bids Dec 10 to import 200,000 tonnes of red and white milling wheat on a three-year credit basis, a grain official said. He said the imports would be from either the U.S., Australia, Argentina or any EU member country.
MARKET TALK - Supplies of soyoil at the U.S. Gulf were said to be tight as dealers scrambled to find enough soyoil to load a vessel set for sail on Dec 12, U.S. exporters said.
